evidence.art: 005-018 film stills are cohesive, painterly, with a strong warm/cool palette and consistent lamp lighting (013, 015, 016). The title (000-003) is rich and period-correct. The painted environments in the walk (028, 038) hold up. The 3D characters are clearly flatter and more game-like than the painted world, so the style is not fully unified.
evidence.continuity: Ankhu's bald head, white kilt and brown sandals hold across 006, 012, 019-049. Anpu's film design (016, 017, 018) has a gold-orange wrapped kilt, a wide blue-gold usekh collar and a bright ankh at hip height. The walk model (030, 032, 038) has a black body, a white kilt and a teal nemes, and the ankh is not readable. Attendants lose their blue-gold collars and sashes (022, 036). The sceptre is thin and often leans or trails (022, 035) instead of standing vertical.
evidence.cinematography_cuts: The film frames are well composed, with a good letterbox, a clear shot order from cradle to old age to dream to Anpu, and a good closing reveal on 018. The walk cuts at 021, 024, 030, 037 and 040 each have a clear subject and strong depth (037 gate, 041 sphinx plinths). Cut 030 to 037 jumps abruptly from far to close. The early high-angle frame 022 has characters cropped against the bottom edge, and the sphinx in the 037 foreground crowds the frame.
evidence.motion_fx: Walk poses read as a stiff cycle. Anpu strides with splayed black legs (028, 022) and the attendants swing their arms identically. Ankhu goes from a neutral stance to a lunge (034 to 035). The fade-out frame 049 is clean. There is no visible foot dust and no flicker. The subtitle fades in and out (031). Pose variety is limited.
evidence.character_grounding: Shadows are cast and oriented to the torches, and the feet touch the paving in most frames (040, 042). Characters are small and sometimes read as pasted onto the painting. Ankhu's kilt has a ragged cut edge (034, 035). Anpu's legs look dark and merge with the cast shadow (038, 039). In 037 and 039 the figures are crammed into the doorway. In the 036 and 038 overhead shots the sphinx scale does not match the walkers.
evidence.game_feel: The route is readable through the torch lines, the pylon in the distance and the lit causeway (019, 038, 040). The cuts follow the party and the pace is calm. At the end the party stops at the gate (046-048) with no clear prompt or goal marker. The party is often small and distant (028-029, 044), which weakens agency.
evidence.ui_title: Gold logo with a wing motif and a clear hierarchy (000). The menu's selected state is clear. Menu text is small and sits low-left over a dark area, so legibility is acceptable but modest. Subtitles are a small serif in white with no backing plate, and they get lost over the bright paving (030-033). The 'The First Gate' card (047-049) is attractive.
evidence.audio_dialogue: Judged from subtitles and frame timing only, since no audio or script file was reviewed. The dialogue ('I served your house for forty years...', 'Your name, at every gate...') is strong and well paced across the cuts. The subtitles line up with the camera changes. Voice quality and mix cannot be judged.

defects.what: Anpu's film design (gold-orange kilt, wide usekh collar, bright ankh) does not match the black-bodied, teal-nemes game model with no readable ankh. Sceptre posture is also inconsistent.
Ankhu's kilt has a ragged edge, the characters crowd the doorway, and the figures read as pasted onto the painted plates. Anpu's dark legs merge with his shadow.
Stiff, repeated walk cycle with splayed legs and a sudden lunge pose, no dust, and no gait variety between Anpu, Ankhu and the attendants.
